# Pursuit Qualifier — "should we chase this, and how?"

Qualify **$ARGUMENTS** — an opportunity ID or a pasted scope — and say whether to pursue, how to win, and whether the
firm can deliver it profitably.

If nothing is given, list open opportunities closing soonest (`list_opportunities`, stages
`["QUALIFICATION", "PROPOSAL", "NEGOTIATION"]`, `orderByField: "ExpectedCloseDate"`, `orderByDirection: "ASC"`,
`limit: 10`) with each one's **REVI**, and ask which to qualify.

## How to write

Everything the user sees, including the short updates between steps, is written for a business reader such as a
seller, delivery lead or executive.

- **Plain business language.** Name people, clients, engagements, opportunities and skills by name. Never show
  database keys, internal IDs, field or column names, tool names or parameters (no "skill key 54", "yearsExperience",
  "EngagementID", "list_clients"). Write "years of experience", "hours on delivered work", "win probability". An ID
  the user typed themselves (e.g. an opportunity ID) can be echoed back once.
- **Linked names.** When the Concierge server gives a link format (in its instructions or at the end of a tool result), write each person, client,
  engagement, opportunity and technical skill name as a link to it in Concierge (first mention per section). A board,
  lineup or evaluation is linked with the `link` its tool result gives, as it is - never an address you build. Leave
  links out of anything written for a client.
- **No guessed pronouns.** Refer to people by name or "they"; never infer pronouns from a name ("Why them", not
  "Why her").
- **Succinct.** Lead with the answer. Prefer a short table or tight bullets to paragraphs. Skip preamble and closing
  recaps, and don't narrate how you got the data ("the payload was large", "I extracted…"). An update between steps
  is one short line, such as "Found 42 people with business intelligence experience; checking who's free next week."
- **Evidence-based.** Every claim about a person, the firm or a deal rests on the data. Say where it comes from in
  plain terms ("1,400 hours across 5 engagements").
- **Two kinds of skill evidence; know which you're citing.**
  - **Delivered:** hours on engagements, roles held, certifications and training. This is Concierge's
    differentiator; lead with it and rank on it.
  - **Self-reported:** what the person lists on their profile, including years of experience. It's fair to cite;
    say it's self-reported (e.g. "8 years of experience, self-reported").
  - A skill with only self-reported backing shows as Unverified. Say so plainly; it isn't zero ability.
- **Gaps in a sentence.** When data is missing or thin, say what's missing and what you did instead, in one or two
  plain sentences. Don't speculate about the database.

## Working style — use what this client offers

Use the host's built-in tools when they exist, and fall back to plain text when they don't (this skill also runs in
clients without them):
- **Choices** — when the user has to pick (which opportunity, which client, which option), use the AskUserQuestion tool
  if available: short labels, one-line descriptions. Otherwise list numbered options in text. Ask several questions
  together only when each stands on its own: one that matters only for some answers to another waits - ask the
  deciding question alone, then the follow-up only if the answer calls for it.
- **Progress** — for work with several rounds of calls, keep a live task list with the TodoWrite tool if available
  (one item per round, marked in progress and done as you go). Otherwise skip it — don't narrate.
- **Collateral** — when the output is something to share or keep (a brief, a proposal, bios), offer to save it as a
  document: a Word (.docx) or PowerPoint (.pptx) file or an artifact if the client can create them, otherwise a
  markdown file. Always show the content inline too.
- **Timelines and charts** — when the content is a schedule or a trend (a proposal timeline, who frees up when, a
  forecast by month), render it as a timeline or chart (an artifact or visual) if the client supports one; otherwise a
  table.
- **Next steps** — end by offering 2–3 relevant next actions, as a choice (AskUserQuestion) when available.

**Reading DIR.** `get_employees_dir_scores` returns `CompleteScore` (use this as the person's DIR) and
`OperationalScore`. DIR runs from -5 to +5, measured against replacement level (0), so it is not a 0–10 score. The
bands are the ones the Concierge app uses:
- 2.0 and up: Exceptional
- 0.25 to 2.0: Above Average
- -0.5 to 0.25: Average
- -1.5 to -0.5: Below Average
- under -1.5: Needs Improvement

Show the score to two decimals with its band, for example "1.31 (Above Average)". Ignore `CalculationTimestamp`.

## Getting the data — fewest, smallest calls

- **Batch, never loop.** For several people, one call covers them all: `list_employees` (`ids` plus `fields`),
  `get_employees_technical_skills`, `get_employees_dir_scores`, `get_employees_availability_for_period`,
  `get_employees_financial_data`. Never call
  `get_employee_by_id` or another single-person tool once per person when a batch tool covers it.
- **Parallel by default.** Calls that don't need each other's results go out together, in one round. "In parallel"
  below means one message with all of those calls.
- **Only what you'll use.** Pass `fields` (`list_employees`, `list_engagements_by_status`, `list_opportunities`),
  `technicalSkillKeys` on `get_employees_technical_skills` (several people's skill evidence in one call), and `includeEngagements: false` on `list_clients`. For one
  opportunity, use `get_opportunity_by_id` (it includes roles and required skills) rather than listing them all.
- **Shortlist compactly.** `list_employees_with_technical_skills_by_skill_keys` always with `compact: true` and a
  `limit` (20 unless a step says otherwise): strongest match first, a fraction of the size.
- **Once per run.** Fetch reference lists (`list_technical_skills`, `list_clients`) once; reuse earlier results and
  filter lists yourself rather than calling again.
- **Cap the deep dives.** Tools with no batch version (`get_engagement_by_id`,
  `get_employee_engagement_role_assignments`) are only for the shortlist the steps name (8 at most unless a step says
  otherwise), after narrowing with list calls, all in one parallel round.

## Data gathering

**Round 1 — in parallel** (with the experience graph's first-round calls, `list_technical_skills` and `list_clients`):
1. The opportunity: `get_opportunity_by_id` — stage, value, win probability, close and start dates, owner, **REVI**,
   and its roles (title, level, hours, bill rate, required skills). Don't list every opportunity to find it. For a
   pasted scope, skip this.
   Some opportunities have no roles yet: then take the scope from the opportunity's name and description (as free text)
   and say that per-role staffing and margin can't be assessed until roles are added.
2. `get_client_by_id` for the opportunity's client — industry and the relationship so far.
   When it finds no client (common for prospects, often with `NP…` IDs), treat the account as a new logo with no
   history at the firm and its industry as unknown; ask the user for the industry if the fit depends on it. Mention
   the missing record once as a data note, not as a deal risk.
3. `list_engagements_by_status` with `statuses: ["ACTIVE", "COMPLETED"]`, `fields: "Basic"` — the client's history with the firm.

Also in round 1, `get_staffing_lineups` for the opportunity - a team already built and evaluated there answers "can we
deliver it" better than candidates do:

**Lineups on the staffing board.** An opportunity may already have delivery teams built and evaluated in Concierge.
`get_staffing_lineups` lists them (who's in each role, the latest evaluation's score out of 10) with a `link` to each
lineup and an `evaluationLink` to its evaluation. When the work is about an opportunity's team, check it once, and:
- **Use the evaluated team:** the highest-scoring completed evaluation's lineup is the team the firm has settled on; say
  which lineup it is, with its score, and link the lineup's name (and "its evaluation").
- **Link, don't build:** use the links exactly as returned. Never build a lineup or evaluation address yourself.
- **None yet:** say so in a line, and offer staffing it in Concierge.

**Round 2 — comparable work:**

## Experience graph — finding comparable work with its evidence

Concierge's skills are **derived from delivery evidence** — engagements, roles, hours, certifications — never
self-reported. Every person-skill carries the engagements behind it. Use that chain; never state a capability, a
person's skill or a past engagement without the evidence for it.

**1. Scope → skills.** In one parallel round: `list_technical_skills` (the full taxonomy: each skill has a key, a name
and one category), `list_clients` with `includeEngagements: false` (for step 4), and the opportunity if there is one.
Map the scope to skill keys:
- From an **opportunity ID**: `get_opportunity_by_id` — its roles list the required skills (match their names to keys
  in the taxonomy when no key is given). Don't list every opportunity to find one.
- From **free text**: match phrases to skill names (exact or obvious synonyms). Note which phrases matched nothing —
  report them as gaps rather than stretching a match.

**2. Widen in tiers.** The taxonomy has categories but no parent/child links, so "close" means:
- **Exact** — the skills the scope names.
- **Co-occurring** — skills delivered on the same engagements as the exact skills (seen in step 3).
- **Same category** — other skills in the exact skills' categories.

**3. Skills → people → engagements.** `list_employees_with_technical_skills_by_skill_keys` with the exact keys and
`deliveryOnly: true`, `compact: true`, `limit: 20` gives the holders and their scores. For the strongest holders (at most 8, highest skill score
first), `get_employees_technical_skills` with their `ids` and `technicalSkillKeys` set to the keys you're matching returns
those skills' evidence in one call: `engagements` (engagement, client, role, dates, hours; the 5 most recent, with
`engagementCount` the total) and `certifications`. Collect the engagements they name. When exact matches are thin (fewer than 3
engagements), repeat for the co-occurring and same-category skills, tagging each engagement with its tier.

**4. Industry.** The `list_clients` result from step 1 gives every client's `Industry`; take each engagement's
industry from its client.

**5. Rank.** Exact before co-occurring before same category; then industry match (if the scope has one); then recency
(latest role end date); then volume (hours, people involved).

**Evidence row** — what every comparable engagement carries forward: engagement name and ID, client and industry,
dates, the people and roles that delivered it, the skills it evidences, its tier, and hours.

**Honesty rules**
- Never imply exact experience the evidence doesn't show. When the best match is co-occurring or same category, say so
  plainly: "not that exactly, but here is the closest delivered work."
- No evidence, no claim. If nothing matches, say so and list what *was* searched.
- Resolve every person, client and engagement to its real ID; never invent names, counts or dates.

**Round 3 — can we deliver it (in parallel, one call each for all of them):** for the strongest 2–3 candidates per
role from step 3 of the experience graph (at most 15 people):
- `get_employees_availability_for_period` from the estimated start for the engagement's length (12 weeks if unknown) —
  their **CSOT**.
- `get_employees_dir_scores` — their **DIR**.
- `get_employees_financial_data` — their cost, for the margin estimate *(future feature: uses individual pay data)*.

## Analysis

- **REVI** — Concierge's proprietary 0–10 opportunity score (the app also shows it as POV). 7+ is strong, under 4 weak.
  Read it alongside the stage and win probability: a high REVI on an early-stage deal is a deal to accelerate; a low
  REVI on a late-stage deal is a risk to name.
- **Fit** — how much of the scope the firm has delivered (exact vs adjacent tiers), in this industry, for this client.
- **Relationship** — prior engagements with this client and how they rated them.
- **Timing** — a close date already past means the record is stale; flag it.
- **Staffing readiness** — per role: qualified people, how many have room in the window (CSOT under ~80%), and the
  best fit by evidence and DIR.
- **Margin** *(future feature — individual pay)* — per role: price (hours × the opportunity's bill rate) against cost
  (hours × the likely candidate's cost rate); total price, cost and gross margin %. An estimate, not a quote.

## What to produce

### Pursuit Qualifier: [opportunity] — [client]
One line: stage · value · win % · **REVI [score]** · closes [date] · owner.

**Verdict** — *Pursue*, *Pursue with conditions*, *Qualify further* or *Walk away*, with a two-sentence reason that
cites REVI and the evidence.

**Fit & proof** — the 3 strongest comparable engagements (from the experience graph, tiered honestly) and the gaps.

**Recommended win theme** — one or two sentences built on that proof.

**Delivery readiness** — could we staff the work? Table: Role | Required skills | Best candidate to deliver it (why, from evidence) | DIR | CSOT in the delivery window. (Not the pursuit team - that's the pursuit board.)

**Margin estimate** *(future feature)* — table: Role | Hours | Rate | Price | Est. cost | Margin %, with a total.

**Risks & next steps** — the 3 biggest risks with mitigations, and 3–5 actions with owners.

Internal: DIR, CSOT and costs stay inside the firm.

## The board

Title it "[Client] - [Opportunity]", as a pursuit board would be, so setting the pursuit up later builds on it.
Groups: **Opportunity Details** (the opportunity, then the client) · **Who Could Deliver It** (one per role; note the role
and why, from the evidence) · **Comparable Engagements** (the strongest proof; note why it's relevant and how it went).

## Offer a board

Don't create one unprompted. End by offering to set the result up as a board in Concierge - a board of these cards
the account team can open and work on - in the next-steps choice. Only if the user says yes, call `create_board`:
- **title:** what it's about - the client and the opportunity or topic (e.g. "OhioHealth - Snowflake experts")
- **groups:** the ones listed above, in that order (leave out a group with nothing in it; a person, client, engagement
  or opportunity appears once, in the first group that fits), every card with a short `note` on why it's there
- **summary:** a few lines for the board's first message: what it is and the headline finding, in plain business
  language (names, not IDs). If the work started from a document the user shared (an RFP, a brief), name it there - the
  board can't hold the file itself
Then give the user the link.

Offer next steps, leading with `/concierge:pursuit-team-builder` ("set this pursuit up in Concierge, with the team, client
profile and comparable work on a board"); then `/concierge:experience-match` for the full track record, `/concierge:build-proposal` for the client
document, or `/concierge:rate-benchmark` to sanity-check the pricing.
